column1: # Operating-system classification for gup's atago end-to-end specs.
# gup's unit tests run on Linux, macOS and Windows, and the E2E suite used to run
# on Linux alone. This file is what keeps the macOS and Windows legs from being an
# unstated subset that quietly shrinks: every spec file is classified, every
# exclusion carries a written reason, and TestOSMatrix_classifiesEverySpec fails
# when a spec is added without a decision.
# Column 1  the spec file, relative to e2e/atago.
# Column 2  the GOOS values it runs on, comma-separated.
# Column 3  why it does not run on the others. Required unless it runs everywhere.
# The recurring Windows reason is worth stating once here. `go install` writes
# "name.exe" into $GOBIN on Windows, and gup takes a package's name straight from
# that file name, so a spec that asserts a $GOBIN path (file: {path: gobin/x}) or
# an exact name in output or gup.json is asserting a POSIX-only string. Making
# those specs run on Windows would mean a second copy of each scenario differing
# only in a suffix, which is duplication rather than coverage: the behavior under
# test (update resolution, pinning, migration, removal) has no OS-specific branch,
# and the .exe normalization those specs would re-cover is already unit-tested in
# internal/binname and cmd. What DOES branch by OS -- the CLI entrypoint, dynamic
# completion, completion install, and the failure contracts -- runs on Windows.
bug_report.atago.yaml
check.atago.yaml
column3: Asserts JSON name fields equal the bare binary name; on Windows every $GOBIN entry is name.exe, so each assertion would need a Windows twin.

column3: Runs everywhere; the POSIX --install scenario carries its own skip and a Windows-only scenario covers the PowerShell install.
